root_motivation: Grounding: explore run explore-20260929T083053Z shows 15 of 168 sessions hitting tenant_key_missing 0.3-5s after signup; the actionable -32602 body is sent as HTTP 401, which the Claude Agent SDK drops, showing only a generic sign-in message. This build confirmed via tests/compat_ac11_ac12_claude_sdk_replay.rs and a full-suite run with legacy session mode enabled that mcphost's transport is fully stateless for the target client: rmcp classifies any initialize as session-based regardless of declared version, and the SDK's own recorded wire shape is indistinguishable from a session-wanting client. Matches the PRD's own exit condition: transport stateless -> blocked; do not substitute a client-supplied identifier.
user_persona: The mcphost end user's agent (Claude Code / Agent SDK) that signs up and calls a host.* tool without repeating tenant_key -- blocked at the transport layer this build. The operator still gets two independent fixes: the journal recording the status a client actually received (AC10), and a regression pin that an anonymous session's refusal shape is unchanged (AC3).

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a streamable-HTTP session that ran signup successfully, When it calls host.catalog.search with no tenant_key and no Authorization header, Then the call succeeds as the new tenant.
Given the session in AC1, When it calls five more host.* tools with no tenant_key, Then every call runs as the bound tenant.

Given a fresh session with no signup, no tenant_key and no header, When it calls host.catalog.search, Then the response is HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate, JSON-RPC -32602, data.error_code tenant_key_missing, byte-for-byte the v0.60.35 body shape.
Given a bound session, an explicit tenant_key of a different tenant wins; an invalid one is refused tenant_key_invalid, not the bound tenant.
Given a bound session, a valid bearer for tenant T2 wins (header wins), and the binding is unchanged for later header-less calls.
Given a session that ran signup twice, a key-less call runs as the second tenant, and the second signup response's session_bound is true.
Given two concurrent sessions, A's calls succeed and B (never signed up) is refused tenant_key_missing; no binding leaks across sessions.
Given 50,000 sessions each running signup, the binding map holds at most 10,000 entries and RSS growth is under 20 MB.
Given a bound session whose tenant is disabled, a key-less call gets TenantDisabled, and the following call gets tenant_key_missing (binding dropped).
Given any tools/call that oauth_401_upgrade rewrites to 401, the request-log line's status field is 401, and for an unmodified 200 response it is 200.
auth_method is session for AC1's call and key for AC4's; healthz's auth block reports session_bound_calls_24h >= 1.
tools/list's tenant_key description states the key is optional on the connection that ran signup; contracts/host-tools.v1.json matches mcphost contract dump.

Given cargo test at the landing commit, every test that passed at v0.60.35 still passes (tkparam/oauthrs suites unchanged) and the sessbind_* tests for the non-deferred ACs pass, gate receipt block=0.

scope: src/http.rs: build_router's two /mcp middleware .layer() calls reordered so oauth_401_upgrade (status rewrite) runs before protocol_version_and_log (the request logger) sees the response -- the only production code change this build makes. legacy_session_mode was tried at true and reverted; the module doc comment still describes today's fully-stateless config.

Cargo.toml/CHANGELOG.md: version bump 0.60.35 -> 0.61.0 (PRD's own version_bump: minor rule) and the CHANGELOG entry recording both the AC10 fix and the AC1/AC2/AC4-AC9/AC11/AC12 deferral with its technical reason.
non_goals: Substituting a client-supplied or TCP-connection-derived identifier for a real transport session id -- the PRD's own technical considerations explicitly forbid this, and mcphost's Caddy reverse-proxy topology (connection pooling to the backend) would make a TCP-connection-identity substitute a cross-tenant binding-leak risk, not just an inferior approximation.

Bumping the rmcp dependency version or patching its session-classification behavior -- SEP-2567's removal of sessions from protocol version 2026-07-28 is a spec-level decision upstream, not a bug a dependency bump would change.
Any change to OAuth, bearer validation, or wrong_tenant semantics for bearer-vs-key conflicts -- PRD's own non-goal, untouched regardless of the deferral.

additional.test_file_names_use_underscores_not_the_: test_prefix sessbind (the PRD's own frontmatter field), same convention as every other test file in this repo.
additional.transport_session_blocker_is_load_bearin: This isn't 'harder than expected' -- it's the PRD's own written exit condition (Technical considerations: 'If mcphost runs the transport stateless (no session id), this PRD is blocked -- record it as blocked with the observation; do not substitute a client-supplied identifier'), confirmed true of this build before any code was written (src/http.rs's shipped with_legacy_session_mode(false)), and confirmed UNFIXABLE within this rmcp integration by the compat_ac11_ac12 regression test's own evidence (see root_motivation) rather than assumed.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't legacy_session_mode(true) just be enabled to get a real Mcp-Session-Id?
five_whys_trace.a: Tried it: a full cargo test run showed 33 pre-existing test failures, all with the same shape -- a request lacking full per-request protocol metadata (which rmcp defaults to protocol version 2025-03-26, itself a legacy/session-eligible version) gets classified as legacy, and lacking an Mcp-Session-Id header, is refused 422 'Unexpected message, expect initialize request' instead of being served statelessly as it is today.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not route only genuinely session-wanting initialize calls to the legacy-mode service and everything else to the existing stateless one?
five_whys_trace.a: rmcp classifies ANY initialize request as legacy-eligible regardless of its declared protocolVersion, and tests/compat_ac11_ac12_claude_sdk_replay.rs proves the real Claude Agent SDK's own initialize call (protocolVersion 2025-11-25) is byte-for-byte the same shape as a client that DOES want a session and never sends Mcp-Session-Id on any later call -- there is no signal in the initialize request itself to route on.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not mint mcphost's own per-connection identifier instead of rmcp's session id?
five_whys_trace.a: The PRD's own non-functional section requires a transport-level, never-client-derived identifier; the only mcphost-visible transport signal weaker than rmcp's own session (e.g. the underlying TCP connection) is already documented elsewhere in this codebase (resolve_source_ip's doc comment) as unreliable in prod, since mcphost runs behind Caddy, which connection-pools to the backend -- two unrelated tenants' calls could share a backend connection, so a connection-identity binding would leak across tenants, violating AC7's own isolation guarantee outright.

five_whys_trace.q: Why defer AC10 and AC3's own delivery works given the same transport is otherwise untouched?
five_whys_trace.a: AC10 (request-log status) and AC3 (anonymous refusal shape) don't depend on any session mechanism existing at all -- AC10 is a pure middleware-ordering fix, and AC3 is already true of today's code with zero changes, so both were safely delivered and tested independently of the blocked mechanism.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does prod issue Mcp-Session-Id today (the PRD's own open question)?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- src/http.rs's shipped StreamableHttpServerConfig sets with_legacy_session_mode(false), which per rmcp's own doc comment means every request is served statelessly regardless of negotiated protocol version. Per the PRD's own technical-considerations sentence, this alone triggers the blocked outcome.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Is enabling legacy session mode acceptable, given the open question defers that judgment to Joe if disabled?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Empirically no, independent of a product judgment call: enabling it regresses 33 already-shipped, must-stay-green tests (AC13's own hard requirement) because rmcp's is_legacy_request classification cannot distinguish the real target client's own wire shape from a client that wants session semantics -- there is no configuration of this build's rmcp integration that adds session support without that regression, so this was not a preference to defer but a build-time fact to report.
